Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed at Band 2, with caveats. ITU/WDI mobile subscriptions per 100 people stood at 38.82 (2022), and GSMA-sourced connections data via DataReportal show growth to an estimated 38-45% by end-2025 depending on the population denominator used (DataReportal's Digital 2026 report implies 44.8%, while a April 2026 Extensia article citing the same 2.49m connections implies 38.1%). These figures measure SIM connections rather than the unique-subscriber metric the variable calls for, and true unique-subscriber penetration is typically lower than connection-based estimates, supporting retention of Band 2. Flagging for human review as the connections trend may already have crossed into the 40-54% band.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
Comments: Law No. 24.001 enacted Jan 2024, DPA to be established
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Law No. 24.001 (Jan 2024) is confirmed enacted, but the independent Data Protection Authority it mandates (due within 12 months, i.e. by Jan 2025) had still not been established as of early 2026; the Ministry of Digital Economy, Posts and Telecommunications acts as interim overseer. Downgraded from 4 to 3 ('legislation enacted but no enforcement authority') to reflect this, since Band 4 specifically requires the DPA to be established.

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: CAR has a comprehensive national off-grid/rural electrification strategy (SNER, 2022-2035) backed by a dedicated implementing agency (ACER) and multiple financed, completed projects (PASEEL, PURACEL, PARSE) delivering mini-grids in Bambari, Berberati, Nola, Bouar, Bossembele and Bangassou plus solar home systems for households, schools and health centres. As of February 2025, these projects had already benefited over 80,000 households across CAR and The Gambia combined, and CAR's 40MW Danzi solar plant has been operational since November 2023. This goes beyond 'active policy with some deployment' and better matches Band 4, 'comprehensive framework with significant deployment'; upgraded from 3 to 4.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited source (Mjengo Hub) is a non-authoritative, likely AI-generated aggregator; its '37.7% solar' claim does not represent total renewable generation share and could not be corroborated by any primary source. World Bank WDI data (EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS, sourced from IEA/UN energy statistics) shows CAR's renewable electricity output at 96.47% of total generation (2021, the latest year available, and stable at 95-99% since 2000), reflecting the grid's near-total dependence on Boali hydropower plus the newer Danzi solar plant. Corrected from Band 2 (10-24%) to Band 5 (75%+).

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The most recent World Bank WDI data (2023) shows urban electricity access at 37.4% and rural access at 2.3%, a gap of approximately 35pp, consistent with the original comment and squarely within the 21-40pp band (3). The original 2022 World Bank press-release source (urban ~35%/rural ~0.4%) is superseded by these more precise 2023 WDI figures, which support the same banding.
